taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-05, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1320.7 | 0.60 | 0.60
2 | 719.2 | 0.46 | 1.06
3 | 872.7 | 0.61 | 1.67
4 | 340.7 | 0.38 | 2.05
5 | 4088.9 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as QQH-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-05, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note – Station T-05, Survey Area T**

The interpreted 5-layer resistivity model shows the following sequence (ohm-m): 1320.7 → 719.2 → 872.7 → 340.7 → 4088.9.

Applying the standard 3-layer curve-type rule to each successive triplet:

- Layers 1-2-3: 1320.7 > 719.2 < 872.7 → **H**
- Layers 2-3-4: 719.2 < 872.7 > 340.7 → **K**
- Layers 3-4-5: 872.7 > 340.7 < 4088.9 → **H**

This gives a curve type of **HKH**, reflecting an initial resistivity decrease, a mid-depth resistive layer, and a final high-resistivity basal layer.

The file classification of **QQH** does not match the computed resistivity sequence (QQH would require a monotonically decreasing trend through the first three layers, which is not observed here). The drilling team should be aware of this discrepancy when referencing the station's curve type in subsurface planning.

Recommend verifying resistivity values and recalculating the curve type before finalizing the interpretation record.

{"curve_type_stated": "HKH", "label_issue_flagged": true}
